sections.heading: Everyday setting
sections.text: Woodside Square Library is explicitly listed inside Woodside Square Mall at 1571 Sandhurst Circle, while Commander Recreation Centre is at 140 Commander Boulevard. Alexmuir Park, Chartwell Park and Brimley Woods add named outdoor destinations within the planning area. The census records both apartment buildings and detached houses, and an average household size of three people. A useful way to explore this setting is therefore to compare the route from a candidate home to the mall library, recreation centre and individual parks, rather than assuming that all of these facilities form one compact centre.

sections.heading: Housing and renting
sections.text: In the 2021 Census sample for Agincourt North, 31.5% of occupied homes were in apartment buildings (excluding duplexes) and 21.5% of households rented. The median monthly shelter cost for occupied rented dwellings was $1,480, including utilities where applicable. This is a historical cost across dwelling sizes, not a budget for a new rental today.

sections.heading: Households and residents
sections.text: The profile counted about 27,540 people in private households and 9,095 households, averaging 3.0 people each. One-person households made up 16.5% of households; children under 15 accounted for 12.3% of residents in private households. These describe the area's residents, not its daytime visitors or a claim that every street has the same household mix.

sections.heading: Resident work profile
sections.text: The three largest broad occupation groups among residents in the 2021 labour force with an applicable occupation were sales and service occupations (30.8%); business, finance and administration occupations (19.2%); trades, transport and equipment operators and related occupations (13.7%). These shares use the census's All occupations total for residents aged 15 and over (25% sample), excluding the Occupation — not applicable category. They describe residents' occupations, not employers, job vacancies or the industries located in Agincourt North; these figures do not identify where residents work.

sections.heading: Parks and public amenities
sections.text: City park polygons overlapping this area include Alexmuir Park; Chartwell Park; Brimley Woods. The mapped Park class covers 3.1% of the planning area's polygon; ravines and other green-space classes can be excluded from that measure. Mapped public amenities inside the planning area include Woodside Square Library; Commander Recreation Centre. Park, library and recreation snapshots were last updated 2026-11-03, 2026-09-22 and 2026-11-01, respectively; check the facility's own listing for hours and programs.

sections.heading: Getting around
sections.text: No scheduled TTC subway station is inside or within 800 m of this area's boundary in this inventory. The feed period is 2026-11-01 to 2026-12-19. It also locates 81 TTC bus stop IDs and 0 streetcar/light-rail stop IDs inside the area; opposite directions can be counted separately. In the pandemic-era 2021 Census, 18.6% of commuting residents used public transit and 3.1% walked or cycled, excluding people working at home.

sections.heading: Practical considerations
sections.text: The census describes a mix of detached homes and apartment buildings, with larger average households and fewer one-person households than several central areas in this set. That is a description of residents, not a rule about who belongs here or what housing is available now. Woodside Square Library, Commander Recreation Centre and the named parks offer specific destinations to test from a prospective address. The scheduled bus-stop count is useful context, but a route map and an actual travel-time check are needed because this inventory does not place a subway station near the planning-area boundary. Treat the 800 m station measure as a distance to the neighbourhood boundary, not a walk from a particular home. Compare the actual address, current rental listings and a trip at the time you would travel before deciding.
